name: Mac Mini M1 (2020)
commonIssues: Internal PSU thermal stress (integrated 150W brick)
Soldered SSD failure - chip-off recovery required
HDMI 2.0 port wear (heavy display swap usage)
Wi-Fi module failure (rare but documented)
Bluetooth dropouts after macOS updates
timelineNotes: Most repairs 1-3 days. PSU same-day to 2 days. Logic-board work 3-5 days.
honestyNote: First Apple Silicon desktop and still excellent value in 2026 for light desktop use. Same chassis as the old Intel Mac Mini, so service is familiar. RAM and SSD are soldered - what you bought is what you keep. We see very few failures on these - they're built well.
heroTagline: First Apple Silicon Mac. Still a brilliant little desktop in 2026 - and we keep them running.

name: Mac Mini M2 (2023)
commonIssues: Slow 256GB base SSD (single NAND chip - performance penalty)
Internal PSU thermal stress
Wi-Fi 6E module dropouts in dense apartment buildings
Bluetooth pairing issues with non-Apple peripherals
HDMI port wear
timelineNotes: Most repairs 1-3 days. Last of the original Mac Mini chassis design.
honestyNote: Last Mac Mini in the original chassis (replaced by the redesigned M4 in Oct 2024). 256GB base model has the well-documented single-NAND slow SSD issue - if performance matters, the 512GB model is much faster.
heroTagline: M2 punch in the classic chassis. Last of its kind before the 2024 redesign.

name: Mac Mini M2 Pro (2023)
chip: Apple M2 Pro (10 or 12-core CPU, 16 or 19-core GPU)
commonIssues: Thunderbolt 4 controller failure under heavy dock load
10GbE port failures (option models)
Internal PSU thermal stress (higher TDP than M2)
HDMI 2.1 port wear with 8K displays
Soldered SSD failure
timelineNotes: Most repairs 2-3 days. First Pro-chip Mac Mini ever - extra Thunderbolt ports versus base M2.
honestyNote: First Pro-chip Mac Mini. Genuinely powerful for the price. Higher TDP than base M2 means the internal PSU works harder - keep airflow around the chassis. We see very few of these come in.
heroTagline: First Pro-chip Mac Mini. 4 Thunderbolt 4 ports, M2 Pro punch.

name: Mac Mini M4 (2024)
ports: Front: 2× USB-C, 3.5mm. Rear: 3× Thunderbolt 4, HDMI, Gigabit Ethernet (10GbE option)
commonIssues: Bottom power button placement (underneath the chassis - controversial)
Front USB-C port wear from heavy plug/unplug cycles
Internal PSU thermal stress in the smaller chassis
HDMI port wear with 4K/8K display swaps
Wi-Fi 6E dropouts in dense apartment buildings
timelineNotes: Replaced by the M6 Mac Mini in August 2026 but still one of the most common minis on Dubai desks. Most parts via authorised channels. Logic-board 3-5 days, PSU same-day to 2 days.
honestyNote: Complete redesign - much smaller (5×5 inches), 16GB base RAM (finally), front USB-C ports. The bottom power button placement (you reach UNDER the Mac Mini) is genuinely awkward but you rarely use it. Excellent value at 16GB base.
heroTagline: Complete redesign. 5×5 inches, front USB-C, 16GB base RAM. Replaced by the M6 mini in August 2026.

name: Mac Mini M4 Pro (2024)
chip: Apple M4 Pro (12 or 14-core CPU, 16 or 20-core GPU)
ports: Front: 2× USB-C, 3.5mm. Rear: 3× Thunderbolt 5, HDMI, Gigabit Ethernet (10GbE option)
commonIssues: Thunderbolt 5 controller heat (new chip generation, runs hot under sustained load)
Front USB-C port wear
Bottom power button placement issue (shared with M4)
10GbE port failures on option models
Internal PSU thermal stress in compact chassis
timelineNotes: Apple's Pro-chip Mac Mini from late 2024 to August 2026 (succeeded by the M5 Pro mini). First desktop with Thunderbolt 5. Logic-board 3-5 days.
honestyNote: First desktop with Thunderbolt 5. 64GB RAM ceiling makes this a serious workstation in a tiny box. Thunderbolt 5 controller runs hot - give it airflow. We're starting to see a few thermal-related issues on heavily-loaded units.
heroTagline: Thunderbolt 5, 64GB capable, M4 Pro. Succeeded by the M5 Pro mini in August 2026.

name: Mac Studio M1 Max (2022)
chip: Apple M1 Max (10-core CPU, 24 or 32-core GPU)
ports: Front: 2× USB-C, SDXC. Rear: 4× Thunderbolt 4, 2× USB-A, HDMI, 10GbE, 3.5mm
commonIssues: Internal fan dust buildup (creative pros run sustained heavy workloads)
Thunderbolt 4 controller failures under heavy dock chains
10GbE port failures
Front SDXC slot wear
Soldered SSD failure (modular SSD board but still keyed to logic board)
timelineNotes: Most repairs 2-4 days. Fan cleaning + thermal paste should be done every 18 months on heavy-use Studios.
honestyNote: First-gen Mac Studio. Built like a tank. The biggest preventive maintenance we recommend is fan cleaning every 18 months - creative workloads coat the fans in dust quickly in Dubai. SSD has a modular daughter board but is keyed to the logic board (Apple's choice - it's not a true upgrade).
heroTagline: First Mac Studio. M1 Max, 64GB capable, built for creative pros.

name: Mac Studio M1 Ultra (2022)
chip: Apple M1 Ultra (20-core CPU, 48 or 64-core GPU - two M1 Max fused)
ports: Front: 2× Thunderbolt 4, SDXC. Rear: 4× Thunderbolt 4, 2× USB-A, HDMI, 10GbE, 3.5mm
commonIssues: Heavy fan dust buildup (Ultra runs hotter than Max)
Thunderbolt 4 controller heat
Internal copper heatsink thermal paste degradation
Front Thunderbolt port wear (Ultra gets TB front, not just USB-C like Max)
10GbE port failures
timelineNotes: Most repairs 2-4 days. Logic-board work 4-6 days (Ultra board is more complex). Fan + thermal service every 12-18 months for heavy users.
honestyNote: First Ultra-chip Mac. Two M1 Max chips fused via UltraFusion interconnect. Runs hotter than M1 Max - service the fans and thermal paste more often. Logic board failures are rare but very expensive (the chip is huge and the board is dense).
heroTagline: Two M1 Max fused. 128GB RAM, 64-core GPU. The first Ultra Mac.

ports: Front: 2× Thunderbolt 5, SDXC. Rear: 4× Thunderbolt 5, 2× USB-A, HDMI, 10GbE, 3.5mm
commonIssues: Thunderbolt 5 controller heat (new chip generation)

10GbE port failures

timelineNotes: Apple's M4 Max Studio (March 2025 - August 2026, replaced by the M5 Max Studio). Most parts via authorised channels. Logic-board 3-5 days. First Studio with Thunderbolt 5.
honestyNote: The M4 Max Studio was replaced by the M5 Max in August 2026, which makes it a strong second-hand buy in Dubai. 128GB RAM ceiling (up from 96GB on M2 Max). Thunderbolt 5 is the headline. For single-threaded work this beats the M3 Ultra; for heavy multi-core the M3 Ultra wins despite being 'older' - see our note on the M3 Ultra page.
heroTagline: Thunderbolt 5, 128GB capable, M4 Max. Replaced by the M5 Max Studio in August 2026.

name: Mac Studio M3 Ultra (2025)
chip: Apple M3 Ultra (32-core CPU, 60 or 80-core GPU - two M3 Max fused)
ports: Front: 2× Thunderbolt 5, SDXC. Rear: 6× Thunderbolt 5, 2× USB-A, HDMI, 10GbE, 3.5mm
commonIssues: Heavy fan dust buildup - 32-core CPU under sustained load is the heaviest desktop workload Apple ships
Thunderbolt 5 controller heat
Internal heatsink thermal paste degradation faster than M2 Ultra under extreme loads
10GbE port failures
Soldered SSD failure (chip-off recovery available)
timelineNotes: Apple's Ultra Studio from March 2025 to August 2026. Logic-board work 4-6 days (Ultra board is the most complex Apple ships). Schedule fan + thermal service every 12 months for heavy users - even sooner for sustained 32-core workloads.
honestyNote: Apple released this in the SAME event as the M4 Max Studio in March 2025 - unusual - and replaced it with the M5 Ultra in August 2026. M3 Ultra has 32 CPU cores vs M4 Max's 16, so for heavy multi-core (3D rendering, scientific compute, large compiles) the 'older' M3 Ultra is faster. For single-threaded work the M4 Max wins. Choose by workload, not chip number.
heroTagline: 32 CPU cores, 512GB RAM ceiling. Apple's most powerful Mac until the M5 Ultra arrived in August 2026.

name: Mac Pro 2019 (Intel Xeon)
ports: 8× Thunderbolt 3 (2 front + 2 rear + MPX modules), 2× USB-A, 2× 10GbE
discontinued: June 2023 (replaced by Mac Pro M2 Ultra)
commonIssues: MPX GPU module failures - Radeon Pro Vega II / W6800X / W6900X (expensive to replace, parts increasingly rare)
Xeon W cooling - thermal paste degradation under sustained 28-core load
1400W PSU failure (rare but catastrophic)
Thunderbolt 3 controller failures across the 8 ports
DDR4 ECC RAM module failures (user-replaceable in 12 slots)
timelineNotes: MPX GPU module replacement is a flat labour fee + the module itself (module prices vary wildly by model - we confirm both in the written quote). PSU 2-3 days. Xeon CPU swaps technically possible but rarely economic in 2026. RAM upgrades same-day.
honestyNote: The 'cheese grater' Mac Pro. PCIe expansion, MPX GPU modules, 1.5TB ECC RAM, 8 Thunderbolt 3 ports - nothing else Apple makes can do this. Apple has not released a true successor (the M2 Ultra Mac Pro lost MPX support). If yours is working, keep it running. We service these professionally with all the genuine Apple parts and MPX modules that are still available.
heroTagline: The cheese grater. PCIe, MPX modules, 1.5TB ECC RAM. Still no true successor in 2026.

name: Mac Pro M2 Ultra (2023)
chip: Apple M2 Ultra (24-core CPU, 60 or 76-core GPU)
commonIssues: Soldered SSD failure - chip-off recovery required (no Apple SSD modules to swap)
Logic board failure is catastrophic - no MPX rescue path
Thunderbolt 4 controller heat across 8 ports
1000W PSU thermal stress
Heavy fan dust buildup in the tower chassis
timelineNotes: Apple discontinued the Mac Pro in March 2026 with no successor - the Mac Studio M5 Ultra is now the top of the range. Logic-board failure is a full-board swap - no PCIe GPU rescue path like the 2019 Intel Mac Pro had. Most repairs 2-5 days; parts stock is still healthy in 2026.
honestyNote: Same tower chassis as the 2019 Intel Mac Pro but with M2 Ultra inside. Apple ended the Mac Pro line in March 2026, so this is the last Mac Pro ever made - which makes long-term repair support (not replacement) the sensible plan. PCIe expansion is gone for GPUs (the GPU is on the SoC). We service both Mac Pro generations - and for extreme RAM and MPX GPU work, the 2019 Intel is still king.
heroTagline: M2 Ultra in the tower. The last Mac Pro Apple made (discontinued March 2026) - we keep it running.
discontinued: March 2026 (Mac Pro line ended - no successor)

name: Mac Mini M6 (2026)
ports: Front: 2× USB-C (10Gb/s), 3.5mm. Rear: 3× Thunderbolt 4, HDMI 2.1, 2.5Gb Ethernet (10GbE option)
commonIssues: Bottom power button placement (same chassis as the M4 mini)
Front USB-C port wear from daily plug/unplug
Wi-Fi 7 / N1 networking teething issues on older routers (usually software, not hardware)
2.5GbE port negotiation faults with older switches
Internal PSU thermal stress in the 5×5-inch chassis
timelineNotes: Apple's current Mac Mini - announced 25 August 2026, on sale 22 September 2026. Brand-new model: check Apple warranty and AppleCare+ before any paid work. Early parts via authorised channels only; logic-board 5-7 days while stock builds.
honestyNote: Same 5×5-inch chassis as the M4 mini - Apple changed the internals, not the box. M6 is Apple's first 2-nanometre chip (12-core CPU vs 10 on M4) and the N1 chip brings Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. Ethernet moved up to 2.5Gb as standard. In its first year almost every fault should go through Apple warranty - we tell you honestly when that is the better route.
heroTagline: Apple's 2026 Mac Mini. M6 (2nm), Wi-Fi 7, 2.5GbE. Same tiny 5×5-inch box.

It replaces the M4 Pro mini one-for-one - if you own an M4 Pro there is no reason to upgrade for repair-related reasons; we support both.
heroTagline: Apple's 2026 Pro mini. M5 Pro, Thunderbolt 5, 64GB capable, Wi-Fi 7.

First-year faults should go through Apple warranty; we check coverage before quoting.

timelineNotes: Apple's current Ultra Studio and the top of the Mac range now that the Mac Pro is discontinued - announced 25 August 2026, on sale 22 September 2026. honestyNote: With the Mac Pro discontinued in March 2026, the M5 Ultra Studio is now Apple's most powerful Mac, full stop. 36 CPU cores, up to 80 GPU cores, 96GB base RAM and a 512GB ceiling (the 512GB build ships from October). Unlike the 2025 lineup - where the M3 Ultra was an older-generation chip than the M4 Max - the M5 Ultra and M5 Max are the same generation, so the Ultra wins on every workload. Warranty-first in year one.
